correctness.rationale: The degree-incidence rules force a perfect matching on all degree-two stubs. The block condition makes the contracted degree-three-center skeleton a tree of degrees one or three; the converse builds exactly the class. Handshake gives orders 8i+8; deletion of leaves bijects these skeletons with subcubic trees on i internal vertices. All graphs at fixed i share a stable (centers,stubs) partition of sizes (2i+2,6i+6) with neighbor-count matrix ((0,3),(1,1)), hence identical C2 theories. The first two internal trees occur at i=4 (P4 and K1,3), proving sharpness within class. Standard-library verifier checks the structural steps and all representatives through i=8 plus explicit pairs through i=29.

value.rationale: This is a complete, natural classification by a minimal two-cell equitable neighbor-count quotient in connected subcubic block graphs, with exact class cardinalities and a sharp first relative C2-isomorphism failure. It proves infinite nonisomorphic examples even though ordinary trees are C2-identifiable; the result exposes why triangle attachments destroy tree rigidity. No claim of a global first threshold is used to inflate value.
